analysis:
The change is documentation only (CHANGELOG.md). The base excerpts (1406-2000) are historical release notes and the head excerpt (1-217) adds the v0.9.21 candidate and unreleased notes. No code or patch hunks were supplied, so the behaviors below are inferred from the changelog prose and are not verified against source.

Security-relevant claims for later passes to verify in the actual code:
(1) Lines 16-19: dev identity with its own paths, labels, keychain items and ports, and cross-install MDM profile acceptance. Check keychain access-group and Secure Enclave key separation (A-002, A-003) and the shared APNs identity (T-042).
(2) Line 21: fan helper v2 keeps per-session leases, reports an older helper, and refuses downgrade. Check T-044, T-046 and T-047, especially lease expiry per session and authentication of the lease holder for both identities.
(3) Lines 25-26: automatic signed and notarized dev releases on master push, with a dev update channel. Check A-011, T-034 and T-013.
(4) Line 20: OOM detection now matches the exact name `darkbloom`.
(5) Lines 30-46: SSD cache write budget raised to 4 TB per day and external cache storage controls. This is consistent with T-041; recheck the endurance and UUID-pinning claims against CacheStorage and CacheVolume.
(6) Line 37: App Attest handling is now processed while model work is suspended. Check the T-053 and T-057 proof, expiry and revocation ordering.
Two low or medium documentation-gap findings were raised. I did not review a code diff.

findings.detail: The changelog says a push to `master` now builds, signs, notarizes and publishes a dev provider release, and that dev providers auto-update to each newer dev build. This adds a CI-driven release path that is not driven by a reviewed tag. It also adds a self-update channel, versions of the form `X.Y.Z-dev.<run>`, and a separate dev coordinator. The threat model's provider binary hash registry (A-011) and the T-034 and T-013 binary-trust analyses assume deliberate, tag-based release registration. Nothing in the visible text says how dev hashes are kept out of the production registry, which signing identity and Team ID dev builds use, or whether a compromised master push can reach prod providers' update path. The note that dev runs receive no `PROD_*` secrets helps, but it is not a registry or identity boundary. Fix: add a threat-model entry, or update T-034 and A-011, covering the dev signing identity, separation of dev and prod registries and update channels, and the branch-protection requirements for the master-push release path.
findings.title: Automatic signed dev provider releases from master pushes are not covered by the threat model

findings.detail: The changelog says a dev and a production provider can run on one Mac. It lists the shared APNs app identity and `DARKBLOOM_*` shell overrides as documented limitations. The T-042 and T-034 challenge model relies on the APNs challenge being bound to the intended provider key and coordinator. A shared APNs identity between a prod-registered and a dev-registered process could let one process receive or observe the other's push-delivered code-identity challenges. The visible text does not say which process the challenge is routed to. Separately, provider OOM detection now matches only the exact process name `darkbloom`, which changes the health signals that feed the provider-instability and watchdog paths (T-043). Fix: state in the threat model that dev and prod must not share APNs token or challenge routing, or document the accepted risk, and note the OOM-signal change as a trust-signal narrowing.
findings.title: Dev and prod providers sharing the APNs app identity, plus an exact-name OOM matcher change, are undocumented in the threat model
